description: Unauthorized EFS Access via Lambda Function Compromise The Lambda function has direct access to EFS through a mounted access point. If compromised through code injection or other means, an attacker could manipulate file operations within the Lambda's permission scope. An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Lambda function's input handling to execute arbitrary file operations on the EFS mount point, potentially accessing or modifying sensitive files.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
mitreATT&CK: T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
recommendation: Implement strict input validation and sanitization in Lambda functions
recommendation: Further restrict EFS access point permissions

description: API Gateway DDoS and Resource Exhaustion Multiple API calls trigger two Lambda functions (API Handler and File Manager), potentially leading to resource exhaustion and increased costs. An attacker scripts automated requests to the API endpoint, causing excessive Lambda invocations and potential service disruption.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement AWS WAF with rate limiting
recommendation: Add request throttling at API Gateway level

description: Insufficient Access Control for File Systems Without proper ACLs tied to Cognito identities, users might access files belonging to other users or outside their permitted scope. A user manipulates file paths or access tokens to access files belonging to another user.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1222 - File and Directory Permissions Modification
